item.description:
960
ACPN50 PHFO 280519

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Karina, located well south-southwest of the southern tip of
the Baja California Peninsula, on Tropical Storm Lowell, located
well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical Storm
Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in a few days. Some gradual development is possible
thereafter and a tropical depression could form during the middle
part of next week while the system moves slowly west-northwestward,
well offshore of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Karina are issued under WMO
header WTPZ31 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP1.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Karina are issued under WMO
header WTPZ21 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP1.

Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Lowell are issued under WMO
header WTPZ32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP2.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Lowell are issued under WMO
header WTPZ22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP2.

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Lala Public Advisory Number 64
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
487 
WTPA32 PHFO 280831
TCPCP2
 
BULLETIN
Post-Tropical Cyclone Lala Advisory Number  64
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
...LALA IS NOW A POST-TROPICAL CYCLONE...
...THIS IS THE LAST NHC ADVISORY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...38.2N 179.4W
ABOUT 680 MI...1095 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 340 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1003 MB...29.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Post-Tropical Cyclone Lala 
was located near latitude 38.2 North, longitude 179.4 West. The 
post-tropical cyclone is moving toward the north-northwest near 6 
mph (9 km/h). A gradual turn toward the west-northwest is expected 
to begin soon, and Lala is forecast to cross the International Date 
line on Friday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Slow weakening is expected, and Lala is forecast to 
dissipate in a couple of days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1003 mb (29.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
This is the last public advisory issued by the National Hurricane 
Center on Lala.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Lala Forecast Discussion Number 64
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTPA42 PHFO 280832
TCDCP2
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Lala Discussion Number  64
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Thu Aug 27 2026

Although Lala is maintaining patches of thunderstorms southeast of
the center, the convective pattern has been disorganized for
nearly a day. Based on the lack of organized deep convection and
because Lala is over cool waters, it is now considered a
post-tropical cyclone. The initial intensity of the system is
estimated to be around 35 kt.
 
The post-tropical cyclone continues to move slowly to the
north-northwest. A gradual turn to the west-northwest or northwest
is forecast as a low- to mid-level ridge becomes better established
to the north of the system. The cyclone is also expected to weaken,
and ultimately dissipate within a couple of days.
 
Lala had lasted about 15 days as a tropical cyclone traveling more
than a couple of thousand miles during that time. This is last
advisory on this system by the National Hurricane Center.

FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  28/0900Z 38.2N 179.4W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROPICAL
